$comment: The showcase agents. `wallet` is filled at key generation, `agentId` after ERC-8004 registration (npm run ops:register in agents/). The dashboard serves each agent's registration document from this file, and the pool grants the agent tier by the id recorded here.

agents.name: Fiyat Nöbetçisi
agents.summary: Forecasts oracle price thresholds by reading the same median the resolver will settle against.
agents.method: Reads the Mento SortedOracles median (a maintained testnet stand-in on Celo Sepolia, where Mento's own feed is over a year stale), measures how far it sits from the market's threshold, and discounts that margin by the time left until settlement. It forecasts drift, not price: agent and resolver read one number, so 'what was the price' is never in dispute.
agents.trustModel: Fully on-chain. Nothing off-chain is believed.
agents.passesWhen: The feed has no reporters, or its median is older than the market's staleness limit — in which case the market is heading for Void anyway.

agents.name: Zincir Nabzı
agents.summary: Forecasts thresholds on Celo's own state by making the exact call settlement will make.
agents.method: Performs the same eth_call the resolver performs, once at the latest block and once ~5000 blocks back, then extrapolates the trend linearly to settlement time. The model is deliberately unsophisticated: the edge is supposed to come from reading real chain data, not from a model nobody can audit.
agents.trustModel: Fully on-chain. Nothing off-chain is believed.
agents.passesWhen: The metric call does not return a clean single word, which is also what makes the resolver void.

agents.name: Skor Kahini
agents.summary: Reports sporting fixtures only when independent public score APIs agree on the exact scoreline.
agents.method: Queries a panel of unaffiliated free score APIs (TheSportsDB, ESPN, and football-data.org when a token is configured), normalises team names across them, and requires a quorum to report the same final scoreline. It does not model unplayed fixtures at all — forecasting a match from no information would be guessing dressed up as research.
agents.trustModel: The one place an off-chain reader is trusted. Requiring several independent sources to agree does not remove that trust, but it turns a single operator's error into a refusal to settle rather than a wrong settlement.
agents.passesWhen: Fewer than the quorum report the match finished, or any source dissents on the scoreline.
